results.title: Dialog boxes appear wrong when using custom Windows UI color schemes [41008801] - Chromium
highlights:
Dialog boxes appear wrong when using custom Windows UI color schemes [41008801] - Chromium
...
UserAgent: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 6.1; WOW64) AppleWebKit/537.31 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/26.0.1410.64 Safari/537.31Steps to reproduce the problem:1. Switch to the High Contrast Windows color scheme (right click on desktop, "Customize", scroll down to get the high contrast schemes)2. Try any kind of dialog box. Example with a Javascript one : http://www.tutorialspoint.com/cgi-bin/practice.cgi?file=javascript_31 What is the expected behavior?Dialog boxes should either :- Not change their font color to match the user'sOR, preferred :- Match the window's background color with the user's.What went wrong?The dialog box appears with white text on white background when using custom color schemes that include a white font. (usually white font on dark background.)Did this work before? Yes Before 26.0.1410.64 mChrome version: 26.0.1410.64 Channel: stableOS Version: 6.1 (Windows 7, Windows Server 2008 R2)This bug is kind of related to this one about drop-down menus : https://code.google.com/p/chromium/issues/detail?id=230258

results.title: 1f0984b [inert] The modal dialog and the fullscreen element should escape inertness of ancestor
highlights:
# 1f0984b [inert] The modal dialog and the fullscreen element should escape inertness of ancestor
...
[inert] The modal dialog and the fullscreen element should escape inertness of ancestor
...
the spec:
...
> While document is so blocked, every node that is connected to
> document, with the exception of the subject element and its flat tree
> descendants, must become inert. subject can additionally become inert
> via the inert attribute, but only if specified on subject itself
> (i.e., subject escapes inertness of ancestors); subject's flat tree
> descendants can become inert in a similar fashion.
...
The modal dialog should escape the inertness set by an ancestor
with the inert attribute. Consider this test case:
 
 find me! 
 
 document.querySelector("dialog").showModal() 

The return value of `window.find('me')` should be true,
because ` ` does not specify the inert attribute.
